idiom_name: typed event union + host job queue / explicit typed array queue
implementation_notes: TypeScript runs on the same event-loop runtime as JavaScript, so the queue itself is still the host's job queue (queueMicrotask/setTimeout/await); the language's contribution is making deferred dispatch safe at compile time by modelling events as a discriminated union whose kind drives exhaustive narrowing in the handler. What replaces the classic structure is the runtime queue plus that union - there is no event hierarchy to write, and the compiler proves every case is handled. An explicit Event[] drained per frame is still the right choice when coalescing or batching must happen at a known point.
pitfalls: Types vanish at runtime: a union-typed queue still accepts malformed payloads arriving from JSON or message events, so validate at the boundary.
One any/unknown cast in a listener registration turns the exhaustive switch back into untyped dispatch; keep strict plus noImplicitAny and a never-checking default branch.
The runtime is JavaScript's: microtask starvation, run-to-completion and the single-threaded drain semantics apply unchanged.
